module_title: Banking and Financial Awareness: Insurance Market and Terminology (Level 3: Advanced)
introduction: At this advanced level, we dissect technical jargon (Actuary, Underwriting), exact FDI limits, the Insurance Ombudsman framework, and the precise numerical data of government-backed insurance schemes. This is highly crucial for RBI Grade B, IBPS PO Mains, and Interview rounds.

core_concepts.title: Technical Jargon: Actuary & Underwriting
core_concepts.description:
- Actuary: A highly specialized mathematician/statistician who calculates risk, life expectancy, and probabilities to determine what the 'Premium' rates should be.
- Underwriting: The formal process by which an insurance company evaluates the risk of insuring a particular person or asset, and decides whether to accept the risk and on what terms.

core_concepts.title: FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) Limits in Insurance
core_concepts.description: The Government of India has increased the FDI limit in Insurance Companies from 49% to 74% (under the automatic route). However, for Insurance Intermediaries (like insurance brokers and third-party administrators), the FDI limit is 100%. For the statutory body LIC, the FDI limit is restricted to 20%.

core_concepts.title: Insurance Ombudsman
core_concepts.description: An alternative dispute resolution forum. If a customer is aggrieved by their insurance company (e.g., unfair claim rejection) and gets no satisfactory reply within 30 days, they can approach the Insurance Ombudsman. The maximum compensation the Ombudsman can award is strictly capped at ₹30 Lakhs.

important_entities.name: Govt Flagship Schemes (PMJJBY & PMSBY)
important_entities.key_fact: The backbone of India's social security for the unorganized sector.
important_entities.significance:
1. PMJJBY (Life Insurance): Age 18-50 years. Premium: ₹436/year. Cover: ₹2 Lakhs.
2. PMSBY (Accidental Insurance): Age 18-70 years. Premium: ₹20/year. Cover: ₹2 Lakhs (for death/full disability) and ₹1 Lakh (for partial disability).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Age Limit Trap for Govt Schemes
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In Mains exams, the age limits of PMJJBY and PMSBY are frequently interchanged in statement questions. Remember: You can buy life insurance (PMJJBY) only up to age 50. But since accidents can happen to anyone at any time, accidental insurance (PMSBY) extends up to age 70.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana) Premium Rates
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Farmers pay heavily subsidized premiums: 1.5% for Rabi crops, 2% for Kharif crops, and 5% for Commercial/Horticulture crops. Students often mix up the Kharif and Rabi percentages.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Rabi is a short word = lowest rate (1.5%). Kharif is a medium word = medium rate (2%). Horticulture is a massive word (and expensive crops) = highest rate (5%).

exam_strategy_tips: For RBI Grade B and PO Interviews, understand the concepts of 'Claim Settlement Ratio' (Percentage of received claims actually paid out by the insurer) and 'Solvency Margin' (The size of an insurer's capital relative to all the risks it has taken).
Always double-check the latest Economic Survey or Budget before your exam for any newly revised premiums (like PMJJBY increasing from ₹330 to ₹436) or updated FDI limits.
